data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

The Titan II that launched Gemini was, like Mercury's rockets, a converted weapon — America's largest intercontinental missile, man-rated to carry a crew. Its defining trait was its fuel: where cryogenic propellants have to be loaded just before launch and can force a scrub, the Titan burned storable liquids that let it sit ready and lift off close to on time. That reliability of timing mattered more than it sounds, because Gemini's whole job was rendezvous, and catching another spacecraft in orbit depends on launching at an exact moment. The workhorse of the program, it flew all ten crewed Geminis without losing a crew.
Titan II GLV is an orbital launcher built by Martin Marietta in USA. Workhorse for Project Gemini. Flew 12 times, 1964–1966.
First crewed Gemini; first orbital maneuver by a crew
14-day endurance flight; rendezvous target for Gemini 6A
First docking of two spacecraft; emergency return
Solved EVA — Aldrin's spacewalks; final Gemini
Two-person crew; rendezvous and EVA practice
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
First US human-rated launcher — variant of the Army's Redstone IRBM. Launched Freedom 7 (1961-05-05) and Liberty Bell 7 (1961-07-21)
1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, Pioneer Venus
Twin-chamber hypergolic first stage that flew every Gemini crew
First-stage section of the Titan II that launched Gemini V (1965)
